components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--on-primary); font-weight: 700; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 1.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary-strong); } .ds-btn-primary:active { box-shadow: var(--shadow-card-pressed); }

components.name: Live Action Button
components.description: Rail Red pill for genuinely live/urgent actions (track a train, view alert).
components.css: .ds-btn-live { background: var(--danger); color: #fff; font-weight: 700; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 1.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-live:hover { filter: brightness(0.9); }

components.name: Departure Card
components.description: The signature artifact: a rounded, elevated card replacing the old ruled table row.
components.html: 07:42London WaterlooPlat 2On time
components.css: .ds-board-card { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:1rem; padding:1rem; border-radius:16px; background:#fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(18,20,28,0.06), 0 6px 16px rgba(18,20,28,0.08); text-decoration:none; color:inherit; } .ds-board-time { font-weight:800; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; font-size:1.3rem; } .ds-board-dest { flex:1; font-weight:600; display:flex; flex-direction:column; } .ds-board-dest small { color:var(--muted); font-weight:400; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Pill status chip, tinted fill, text always states the condition.
components.css: .ds-chip { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:0.3rem; font-size:0.78rem; font-weight:700; padding:0.2rem 0.65rem; border-radius:999px; } .ds-chip-ok { color:#076d3a; background:#e6f6ee; } .ds-chip-live { color:#a91824; background:#fceaeb; }

components.name: Bottom Tab Bar
components.description: Signature mobile navigation: fixed bottom bar, 5 destinations, icon+label, red live-alert dot badge.

components.css: .ds-tabbar { position:fixed; bottom:0; left:0; right:0; display:flex; background:#fff; box-shadow:0 -1px 0 var(--border), 0 -8px 24px rgba(18,20,28,0.06); padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom); } .ds-tab { flex:1; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; gap:0.15rem; padding:0.5rem 0; font-size:0.68rem; font-weight:600; color:var(--muted); text-decoration:none; position:relative; min-height:48px; } .ds-tab-active { color:var(--primary); } .ds-tab-badge { position:absolute; top:0.35rem; right:calc(50% - 1.1rem); width:0.45rem; height:0.45rem; border-radius:50%; background:var(--danger); border:1.5px solid #fff; }

components.name: Double-Arrow Mark
components.description: The British Rail symbol, two-tone: upper arrow Rail Blue, lower arrow Rail Red — the one place the duotone literally joins.
components.html: Mainline

narrative.overview: Mainline reads as a native transit app rather than a printed identity manual: a bold red/blue duotone on white, used as two confident equal partners, with soft rounded cards and real elevation replacing the previous ruled hairline tables, and a bottom tab bar on mobile. Blue is calm and structural (navigation, primary action, focus). Red is live and urgent (delays, alerts, countdowns). The double-arrow carries forward as the one piece of heritage, now drawn two-tone where blue and red literally meet.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, light-first; red and blue both carry real UI weight (duotone, not one-accent).
Cards, not hairline tables — the departure board is a stack of rounded rows with real elevation.
Bottom tab bar for primary navigation on mobile; the desktop header keeps a slimmer top bar.
Generously rounded corners (10-22px) everywhere; pill-shaped primary buttons and status chips.
Inter throughout, tabular figures for times; weight and size carry hierarchy.

rules.name: The Two-Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue and red are the only saturated colours doing brand work. Blue is calm and structural; red is live and urgent. Neither decorates a panel for its own sake.

rules.name: The Signal-Text Rule
rules.body: Colour never stands alone on live status: a chip or label always states the condition in words alongside its colour.

rules.name: The Real-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Every card carries the rest shadow; nothing sits flush with the grey surface except the surface itself and true full-bleed sections.

dos: Do use both blue and red as real UI colours — blue for structure/navigation/primary action, red for live/urgent/alerts.
Do build the departure board and journey results as a card stack with real elevation, not a ruled table.
Do give mobile a fixed bottom tab bar with icon + label and a red live-alert dot.
Do round every corner generously — pill buttons/chips, 16px cards, 10px inputs.
Do keep every signal chip paired with text stating the condition.
donts: Don't reduce back to one rare institutional accent colour — this world is a confident duotone.
Don't flatten cards to hairline-only structure; every card needs a visible rest shadow.
Don't square off corners again; pill/16px/10px is the form language now.
Don't literally reproduce the real Great British Railways mark or claim official affiliation.
Don't reintroduce the previous world's violet accent, dark-by-default, or decorative gradients/glows.
